claims.claim: In the medaka myotome, chains of individual sarcomeres were observed with mNG-myosinhc labeling the Myosin A band inside each sarcomere.
claims.source: In the medaka myotome, we were able to observe mNG-myosinhc chains of individual sarcomeres (A-bands separated by the I-bands), indicating that tagged Myosinhc is incorporated correctly in muscle fibers (Taylor et al., 2015; Loison et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citations to prior work on sarcomere structure.

claims.claim: The mNG-myosinhc line enables the in vivo recording of endogenous Myosinhc dynamics during muscle growth for the first time in a vertebrate model.
claims.source: We use this line to record the endogenous dynamics of Myosinhc during muscle growth in vivo for the first time to the best of our knowledge, in a vertebrate model (Video 6, n = 9 embryos).
claims.evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claims.claim: Cadherins are a highly conserved class of transmembrane proteins that are essential components of cell–cell adhesion and are expressed on cellular membranes.
claims.source: Cadherins are a highly conserved class of transmembrane proteins that are essential components of cell–cell adhesion and are thus expressed on cellular membranes (Leckband and de Rooij, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: A large number of cadherin genes exist in vertebrates where they exhibit tissue-specific expression patterns and are implicated in various developmental processes.
claims.source: A large number of cadherin genes exist in vertebrates where they exhibit tissue-specific expression patterns and are implicated in various developmental processes (Halbleib and Nelson, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: The C-terminus of medaka cadherin 2 (cdh2, n-cadherin) was tagged with eGFP.
claims.source: We decided to tag the C-terminus of medaka cadherin 2 (cdh2, n-cadherin) with eGFP.
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claims.claim: cdh2 is known to be expressed primarily in neuronal tissues in a number of vertebrates.
claims.source: cdh2 is known to be expressed primarily in neuronal tissues in a number of vertebrates (Harrington et al., 2007; Suzuki and Takeichi, 2008).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The cdh2-eGFP KI line shows cellular membrane expression in a variety of neuronal and non-neuronal tissues including the spinal cord, the eye, and the notochord.
claims.source: The cdh2-eGFP KI line shows cellular membrane expression in a variety of neuronal and non-neuronal tissues including the spinal cord, the eye, and the notochord (Figure 2E, n = 5 embryos) and neuromasts of the lateral line (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, n = 5 embryos, Video 7,  n = 3 embryos), in addition to the developing heart (data not shown) (Chopra et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claims.claim: The high expression of cdh2 in both differentiated notochord cell types has not been previously reported in medaka but is not unexpected as this tissue experiences a high level of mechanical stress and requires strong cell–cell adhesion.
claims.source: The high expression of cdh2 in both differentiated notochord cell types (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3) has not been previously reported in medaka but is not unexpected as this tissue experiences a high level of mechanical stress and requires strong cell–cell adhesion (Lim et al., 2017; Adams et al., 1990; Garcia et al., 2017; Seleit et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citations to prior work on notochord mechanics.

claims.claim: The cdh2-eGFP KI can be used to study dynamics of n-cadherin distribution in vivo during vertebrate embryogenesis.
claims.source: The cdh2-eGFP KI can be used to study dynamics of n-cadherin distribution in vivo during vertebrate embryogenesis (Video 8, n = 2 embryos).
claims.evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claims.claim: Microtubule plus-end binding proteins are conserved regulators of microtubule dynamics, acting as a scaffold to recruit several additional proteins to ensure essential cell functions such as cell polarity, intra-cellular transport, and mitosis.
claims.source: Microtubule plus-end binding proteins are conserved regulators of microtubule dynamics, acting as a scaffold to recruit several additional proteins to ensure essential cell functions such as cell polarity, intra-cellular transport, and mitosis (Nehlig et al., 2017; Tirnauer and Bierer, 2000; Galjart, 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The microtubule plus-end binding protein mapre1b (eb1) was successfully targeted, generating a C-terminal fusion protein with mScarlet.
claims.source: We successfully targeted the microtubule plus-end binding protein mapre1b (eb1), generating a C-terminal fusion protein with mScarlet.
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claims.claim: mapre1b-mScarlet is widely expressed in medaka embryos: epithelial cells, muscle cells, the notochord, and neuromasts all show mapre1b-mScarlet expression, with the highest level of expression occurring in the spinal cord.
claims.source: mapre1b-mScarlet is widely expressed in medaka embryos: epithelial cells, muscle cells, the notochord, and neuromasts all show mapre1b-mScarlet expression (Figure 2G, Video 9, n = 5 embryos), the highest level of expression occurs in the spinal cord (Figure 2G, yellow arrowhead).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claims.claim: Microtubule dynamics in the spinal cord of living embryos were recorded using the mapre1b-mScarlet line.
claims.source: We were also able to record microtubule dynamics in the spinal cord of living embryos (Video 10, n = 5 embryos) highlighting the utility of this line for exploring the dynamics of microtubules in vivo during development.
claims.evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claims.claim: The novel mScarlet-pcna line can act as an organismal-wide bona fide marker for the location of proliferative cells within any tissue or organ of interest.
claims.source: We reasoned that the novel mScarlet-pcna line can act as an organismal-wide bona fide marker for the location of proliferative cells within any tissue or organ of interest.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the properties of Pcna.

claims.claim: Double transgenic animals were generated with eGFP-cbx1b as a ubiquitous nuclear marker and mScarlet-pcna as a label for cycling cells.
claims.source: We therefore decided to generate double transgenic animals with eGFP-cbx1b as a ubiquitous nuclear marker and mScarlet-pcna as a label for cycling cells (Figure 3).
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claims.claim: Neuromasts are small rosette shaped sensory organs located on the surface of teleost fish that sense the direction of water flow and relay the information back to the central nervous system.
claims.source: Neuromasts are small rosette shaped sensory organs located on the surface of teleost fish that sense the direction of water flow and relay the information back to the central nervous system (Seleit et al., 2017a; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015; Jones and Corwin, 1993; Wada et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Neuromasts consist of four cell types: differentiated hair cells (HCs) in the very centre, underlying support cells (SCs), a ring of mantle cells (MCs), and neuromast border cells (nBCs).
claims.source: They consist of four cell types: differentiated hair cells (HCs) in the very centre, underlying support cells (SCs), a ring of mantle cells (MCs), and neuromast border cells (nBCs) (Seleit et al., 2017b; Dufourcq et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Previous work in medaka has established MCs to be the true life-long neural stem cells within mature neuromast organs.
claims.source: Previous work in medaka has established MCs to be the true life-long neural stem cells within mature neuromast organs (Seleit et al., 2017b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: eGFP-cbx1b labels all neural cells within a mature neuromast organ (HCs, SCs, and MCs).
claims.source: While the eGFP-cbx1b labels all neural cells within a mature neuromast organ (HCs, SCs, and MCs) (Figure 3A), mScarlet-pcna expression matches the previously reported location of proliferative MCs (Seleit et al., 2017b; Figure 3A'–A'', white arrowhead).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: mScarlet-pcna expression matches the previously reported location of proliferative MCs in neuromasts.
claims.source: While the eGFP-cbx1b labels all neural cells within a mature neuromast organ (HCs, SCs, and MCs) (Figure 3A), mScarlet-pcna expression matches the previously reported location of proliferative MCs (Seleit et al., 2017b; Figure 3A'–A'', white arrowhead).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A' and citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Neither the differentiated HCs nor the SCs directly surrounding them show evidence of Pcna expression in mature neuromast organs under homeostatic conditions in medaka.
claims.source: Neither the differentiated HCs nor the SCs directly surrounding them show evidence of Pcna expression in mature neuromast organs under homeostatic conditions in medaka (Figure 3A–A'', n = 10 neuromast organs).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The results validate the utility of mScarlet-pcna as an in vivo marker of proliferative cells.
claims.source: Our results validate the utility of mScarlet-pcna as an in vivo marker of proliferative cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the neuromast data.

claims.claim: nBCs are induced to form from epithelial cells that come into contact with neuromast precursors during organ formation and these induced cells become the stem cell niche of mature neuromast organs.
claims.source: Previous work has shown that nBCs are induced to form from epithelial cells that come into contact with neuromast precursors during organ formation and that these induced cells become the stem cell niche of mature neuromast organs (Seleit et al., 2017b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: nBCs (4/42) in late S phase of the cell cycle were observed in mature neuromast organs, as evident by the presence of nuclear speckles.
claims.source: Utilizing the mScarlet-pcna line we were able to observe nBCs (4/42) in late S phase of the cell cycle, as evident by the presence of nuclear speckles, in mature neuromast organs (Figure 3A'–A'', yellow arrowheads).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A'.

claims.claim: The observation of nBCs in late S phase provides direct evidence that nBCs retain the ability to divide and are thus not post-mitotic cells.
claims.source: This provides direct evidence that nBCs retain the ability to divide and are thus not post-mitotic cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of cycling nBCs.

claims.claim: Proliferative cells in the optic tectum of medaka are located at the lateral, caudal, and medial edge of the tectum in a crescent-like topology.
claims.source: We show that proliferative cells in the optic tectum of medaka are located at the lateral, caudal, and medial edge of the tectum in a crescent-like topology (Figure 3B–B'', n = 4 embryos).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: mScarlet-pcna expression is graded in the optic tectum, with the more central cells gradually losing expression of Pcna.
claims.source: Moreover, mScarlet-pcna expression is graded, with the more central cells gradually losing expression of Pcna (Figure 3B').
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B'.

claims.claim: The observed proliferation pattern in the optic tectum is in line with previous histological findings using BrdU/IdU stainings in similarly staged medaka embryos.
claims.source: This is in line with previous histological findings using BrdU/IdU stainings in similarly staged medaka embryos (Nguyen et al., 1999; Alunni et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Cells located proximally in the developing pectoral fin expressed the highest levels of mScarlet-pcna, with mScarlet-pcna expression decreasing gradually along the proximo-distal axis.
claims.source: We found that cells located proximally expressed the highest levels of mScarlet-pcna, with mScarlet-pcna expression decreasing gradually along the proximo-distal axis (Figure 3C').
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C'.

claims.claim: The proliferation pattern in the pectoral fin has not been previously reported and provides evidence that the differentiation axis of the pectoral fin is spatially organized from proximal to distal in medaka.
claims.source: To the best of our knowledge this proliferation pattern has not been previously reported and our data provide evidence that the differentiation axis of the pectoral fin is spatially organized from proximal to distal in medaka.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observed proliferation pattern.

claims.claim: Proliferative cells are present in the spinal cord of stage 40 medaka embryos, and these mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells occur in clusters preferentially located on the dorsal side of the spine.
claims.source: Lastly, we reveal that proliferative cells are present in the spinal cord of stage 40 medaka embryos, a finding that has not been previously reported, and we show that these mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells occur in clusters preferentially located on the dorsal side of the spine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, n = 4 embryos).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The mScarlet-pcna line acts as a stable label of proliferative cells and can be used to uncover the location of proliferation zones in vivo within organs or tissues of interest in medaka.
claims.source: The newly developed mScarlet-pcna line therefore acts as a stable label of proliferative cells and as such can be used to uncover the location of proliferation zones in vivo within organs or tissues of interest in medaka.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the characterization data.

claims.claim: Endogenously tagged Pcna can be used to determine all cell cycle phases based on the fact that both the levels and dynamic distribution of Pcna show reproducible characteristics in each phase of the cell cycle.
claims.source: In addition to its use as a marker for cells in S phase, it has been shown that endogenously tagged Pcna can be used to determine all other cell cycle phases. This is based on the fact that both the levels and dynamic distribution of Pcna show reproducible characteristics in each phase of the cell cycle (Held et al., 2010; Piwko et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2015; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Leonhardt et al., 2000; Leung et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle have been shown to decrease the levels of Pcna within the nucleus over time.
claims.source: Cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle have been shown to decrease the levels of Pcna within the nucleus over time (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 11, n = 9 epithelial cells) (Zerjatke et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Cells progressing through to S phase have been shown to increase the levels of Pcna expression within the nucleus over time.
claims.source: On the other hand, cells progressing through to S phase have been shown to increase the levels of Pcna expression within the nucleus over time (Leonhardt et al., 2000; Piwko et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2011; Santos et al., 2015; Barr et al., 2016; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Held et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: All tracked epithelial cells that eventually underwent a cellular division showed an increase in nuclear intensity of mScarlet-Pcna prior to the appearance of nuclear speckles.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that all tracked epithelial cells that eventually underwent a cellular division showed an increase in nuclear intensity of mScarlet-Pcna prior to the appearance of nuclear speckles (Figure 4A–B'', Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 12, n = 9 epithelial cells).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claims.claim: Nuclear speckles of Pcna mark the presence of replication foci in late S phase of the cell cycle.
claims.source: Nuclear speckles of Pcna mark the presence of replication foci in late S phase of the cell cycle (Leonhardt et al., 2000; Piwko et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2011; Barr et al., 2016; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Held et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The S/G2 transition can be identified as the point of peak pixel intensity distribution of endogenous Pcna within the nucleus.
claims.source: Previous work has also shown that the S/G2 transition can be identified as the point of peak pixel intensity distribution of endogenous Pcna within the nucleus (Zerjatke et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: The peak pixel intensity distribution within nuclei was determined by a combination of 3D surface plots and histograms of pixel intensity distributions over time.
claims.source: We were are able to determine the peak pixel intensity distribution within nuclei by a combination of 3D surface plots and histograms of pixel intensity distributions over time (Figure 4B–D, Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3, and Videos 12–14, n = 9 epithelial cells).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claims.claim: Onset of M phase is marked by a sharp decrease in nuclear levels of Pcna.
claims.source: Finally, onset of M phase is marked by a sharp decrease in nuclear levels of Pcna (Zerjatke et al., 2017; Leung et al., 2011; Piwko et al., 2010; Held et al., 2010), which we could consistently detect in the endogenous mScarlet-Pcna intensity tracks of epithelial cells undergoing division (Figure 4A–C, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2, and Videos 12–14, n = 9 epithelial cells).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The mScarlet-pcna line recapitulates known dynamics of Pcna within the nucleus and can be utilized as an endogenous 'all-in one' cell cycle reporter in vertebrates.
claims.source: We therefore provide initial evidence that the mScarlet-pcna line recapitulates known dynamics of Pcna within the nucleus (Held et al., 2010; Piwko et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2015; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Barr et al., 2016; Leonhardt et al., 2000; Leung et al., 2011) and that it can therefore be utilized as an endogenous 'all-in one' cell cycle reporter in vertebrates.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the characterization data and citations to prior work.

claims.claim: There is still a paucity of precise, single-copy fusion protein lines in vertebrates, in general, and in teleost fish in particular.
claims.source: Despite the CRISPR/Cas9 system being repurposed as a broad utility genome editing tool almost a decade ago (Jinek et al., 2012; Cong et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2016) and despite its revolutionary impact as a method to generate knock-ins by HDR (Danner et al., 2017; Jasin and Haber, 2016; Ceccaldi et al., 2016; Lisby and Rothstein, 2004), there is still a paucity of precise, single-copy fusion protein lines in vertebrates, in general, and in teleost fish in particular.
claims.evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field supported by citations.

claims.claim: In medaka there are a total of three validated single-copy fusion protein lines by CRISPR/Cas9 reported prior to this work.
claims.source: In fact, in medaka there are a total of three validated single-copy fusion protein lines by CRISPR/Cas9 reported prior to this work (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018), and in zebrafish, a handful of lines have been reported so far (Wierson et al., 2020; Hisano et al., 2015; Auer et al., 2014; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The limited number of validated lines underscores the complexity of generating and validating precise single-copy fusion protein KI lines in teleost models.
claims.source: This underscores the complexity of generating and validating precise single-copy fusion protein KI lines in teleost models.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the paucity of lines.

claims.claim: Previous techniques to generate large KIs required the usage of plasmid vectors commonly containing long homology arms (>200 bp).
claims.source: Previous techniques to generate large KIs (such as fluorescent reporters) required the usage of plasmid vectors commonly containing long homology arms (>200 bp) (Zu et al., 2013; Shin et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Problems arising during and after injection include DNA concatemerization of the donor construct.
claims.source: Problems arising during and after injection include DNA concatemerization of the donor construct (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Auer et al., 2014; Winkler et al., 1991; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2014), in addition to possible imprecise and off-target integration of either the fluorescent protein sequence or the plasmid backbone (Auer et al., 2014; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Won and Dawid, 2017; Wierson et al., 2020; Shin et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2013; Hackett et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work documenting these issues.

claims.claim: The vast majority of reported HDR-mediated knock-ins in teleosts rely on in vivo linearization of the plasmid donors.
claims.source: The vast majority of reported HDR-mediated knock-ins in teleosts rely on in vivo linearization of the plasmid donors.
claims.evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field.

claims.claim: Linear dsDNA donors can drive HDR but might be prone to degradation, concatemerization, and are generally thought to be more toxic than plasmid donors.
claims.source: This strategy is utilized due to the observation that, although linear dsDNA donors can drive HDR, they might be prone to degradation, concatemerization, and are generally thought to be more toxic than plasmid donors (Auer et al., 2014; Cristea et al., 2013; Auer and Del Bene, 2014; Hisano et al., 2015; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Wierson et al., 2020; Yao et al., 2017; Winkler et al., 1991).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Plasmid donors contain an additional guide RNA sequence to drive in vivo linearization in order to synchronize the availability of the linear DNA donor with Cas9 activity.
claims.source: Plasmid donors therefore contain an additional guide RNA sequence to drive in vivo linearization in order to synchronize the availability of the linear DNA donor with Cas9 activity (Auer et al., 2014; Cristea et al., 2013; Hisano et al., 2015; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019; Wierson et al., 2020; Yao et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Directly injecting PCR-amplified linear DNA with short homology arms (~35 bp) could be highly effective since these donors are relatively small (~780 bp) compared to plasmids (several kbs), and therefore a small quantity of donors (~10 ng/µl) will provide a large number of molecules (~20 nM) available to engage the HDR machinery following the Cas9-induced DSB.
claims.source: We reasoned that directly injecting PCR-amplified linear DNA with short homology arms (~35 bp) could be highly effective since these donors are relatively small (~780 bp) compared to plasmids (several kbs), and therefore a small quantity of donors (~10 ng/µl) will provide a large number of molecules (~20 nM) available to engage the HDR machinery following the Cas9-induced DSB.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on molecular considerations.

claims.claim: 5′ biotinylated primers were used in order to limit in vivo concatemerization of the donor construct.
claims.source: Building on recent improvements in CRISPR/Cas9 KI strategies, we used 5′ biotinylated primers in order to limit in vivo concatemerization of the donor construct (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018), and synthetic sgRNAs were used to increase the efficiency of DSBs by Cas9 (Paix et al., 2015; Kroll et al., 2021; Hoshijima et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citation.

claims.claim: Synthetic sgRNAs were used to increase the efficiency of DSBs by Cas9.
claims.source: Building on recent improvements in CRISPR/Cas9 KI strategies, we used 5′ biotinylated primers in order to limit in vivo concatemerization of the donor construct (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018), and synthetic sgRNAs were used to increase the efficiency of DSBs by Cas9 (Paix et al., 2015; Kroll et al., 2021; Hoshijima et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citations.

claims.claim: A monomeric streptavidin-tagged Cas9 was utilized that has a high affinity to the biotinylated donor fragments to increase targeting efficiency.
claims.source: In addition, we utilized a monomeric streptavidin-tagged Cas9 that has a high affinity to the biotinylated donor fragments to increase targeting efficiency (Gu et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citation.

claims.claim: The benefit of using the mSA/Biotin system to increase targeting efficiency in F0 needs to be further evaluated.
claims.source: While 7/8 KI lines were generated and validated using Cas9 mSA and 5′ biotinylated donor fragments, the benefit of using the mSA/Biotin system to increase targeting efficiency in F0 needs to be further evaluated: in our initial comparison, using (2xNLS) Cas9 with and without mSA, and repair donors with and without biotinylation, we have found a comparable lethality and mosaic KI efficiency rates in F0s (Supplementary file 3g).
claims.evidence: This is based on experimental comparison data.

claims.claim: Cas9 containing only one NLS and no mSA showed a lower lethality rate and a lower mosaic KI efficiency in F0s compared to Cas9 with two NLSs.
claims.source: We also tested another Cas9 containing only one NLS and no mSA (Gagnon et al., 2014) and found a lower lethality rate and a lower mosaic KI efficiency in F0s compared to Cas9 with two NLSs (Supplementary file 3g).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental comparison data.

claims.claim: The approach reported is a highly efficient, precise, and scalable strategy for generating single-copy fusion proteins.
claims.source: Irrespective of these considerations, the approach reported here is a highly efficient, precise, and scalable strategy for generating single-copy fusion proteins (Supplementary files 3g and 4).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: The fact that the repair donors are synthesized by PCR amplification eliminates the need for both cloning and a second guide RNA for in vivo linearization.
claims.source: The fact that the repair donors are synthesized by PCR amplification eliminates the need for both cloning and a second guide RNA for in vivo linearization.
claims.evidence: This describes an advantage of the methodology.

claims.claim: The strategy significantly simplifies the process of endogenous protein tagging in a vertebrate model.
claims.source: Therefore, the strategy we utilize significantly simplifies the process of endogenous protein tagging in a vertebrate model.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the methodological advantages.

claims.claim: A similar approach to the one presented showed the potential to generate CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KI lines in zebrafish by targeting non-coding genomic regions with PCR-amplified donor constructs.
claims.source: Very recently a similar approach to the one we present here showed the potential to generate CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KI lines in zebrafish by targeting non-coding genomic regions with PCR-amplified donor constructs (Levic et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to recent work.

claims.claim: The work in zebrafish together with the present work in Medaka supports the notion that donors with short homology arms are sufficient to drive HDR when they are in the form of linear dsDNA.
claims.source: Together with our present work in Medaka, this supports the notion that donors with short homology arms are sufficient to drive HDR when they are in the form of linear dsDNA.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the current work and recent zebrafish work.

claims.claim: Following the Cas9-induced DSB, the donor may be integrated by synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA).
claims.source: One possible explanation is that following the Cas9-induced DSB, the donor is integrated by synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA).
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis about the mechanism.

claims.claim: During SDSA, the 3′ ends of chromosomal DNA strands at the DSB can anneal with the repair donor and drive its replication and insertion at the site of the DSB.
claims.source: During SDSA, the 3′ ends of chromosomal DNA strands at the DSB can anneal with the repair donor and drive its replication and insertion at the site of the DSB (Lisby and Rothstein, 2004; Danner et al., 2017; Jasin and Haber, 2016; Ceccaldi et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on SDSA mechanisms.

claims.claim: Short homologies (30–40 bp) appear to be sufficient to anneal with chromosomal DNA and engage the SDSA machinery.
claims.source: Short homologies (30–40 bp) appear to be sufficient to anneal with chromosomal DNA and engage the SDSA machinery (Paix et al., 2017a, Paix et al., 2016; Grzesiuk and Carroll, 1987).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The validation process of single-copy insertions is complicated in approaches that use long homology arms (>200 bps) to generate knock-ins as concatemerization and the formation of episomes cannot be easily ruled out.
claims.source: An important aspect of any KI strategy to generate fusion proteins is its precision. The validation process of single-copy insertions is complicated in approaches that use long homology arms (>200 bps) to generate knock-ins as concatemerization (Winkler et al., 1991; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018) and the formation of episomes (Aljohani et al., 2020; Wade-Martins et al., 1999; Udvadia and Linney, 2003; Winkler et al., 1991; Wierson et al., 2020) cannot be easily ruled out.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work documenting these issues.

claims.claim: Locus genotyping by PCR and Sanger sequencing is difficult when using primers external to the repair donor due to the large size of the expected fragment and competition for amplification with the wildtype allele.
claims.source: Locus genotyping by PCR and Sanger sequencing is difficult when using primers external to the repair donor due to the large size of the expected fragment and competition for amplification with the wildtype allele.
claims.evidence: This describes a technical challenge with long homology arms.

claims.claim: Internal primers within the donor (junction PCR) have been used to avoid the limitation of large fragment size, but this can lead to PCR artefacts and crucially, it does not rule out concatemerization of the injected dsDNA.
claims.source: Internal primers within the donor (junction PCR) have been used to avoid this limitation, but this can lead to PCR artefacts and crucially, it does not rule out concatemerization of the injected dsDNA (Won and Dawid, 2017; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Auer et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Southern blotting is considered the gold standard to assess single-copy integration.

results.result: A simplified, highly efficient CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in strategy was established in medaka using PCR-amplified donor fragments with short homology arms (30-40 bp), biotinylated 5' ends, and Cas9-mSA. Eight genes were targeted with various fluorescent proteins, achieving F0 targeting efficiency of 11-59% mosaic expression and germline transmission of 25-100%. Eight stable KI lines were established, with 7/8 requiring only a single injection round.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C32 collectively demonstrate the establishment and efficiency of the method through experimental data showing successful generation of multiple lines with quantified targeting and germline transmission rates (C23, C25, C26, C27, C28). Control experiments (C24) validate the requirement for homology arms. The methodology is well-documented (C4, C14, C18-C21) and advantages are clearly stated (C20, C21, C32).

results.result: Initial comparison of different Cas9 designs (with/without mSA tag, with/without biotinylation) showed comparable KI efficiencies in F0s. Cas9 with only one NLS showed lower efficiency and lethality compared to Cas9 with two NLSs.
results.evaluation: Claims C30, C124, C125 present preliminary comparative data but acknowledge that further evaluation is needed (C124). The comparison is described as 'initial' with limited scope (F0 screening only), and the authors explicitly state the benefit of the mSA/Biotin system needs further evaluation. Sample sizes and statistical analysis are not provided.

results.result: Whole genome sequencing with high coverage and Sanger sequencing validated precise single-copy integration at targeted loci. WGS of three lines (eGFP-cbx1b, mScarlet-pcna, mNeonGreen-myosinhc) showed fluorescent protein reads only at endogenous target loci. Sanger sequencing of seven lines confirmed in-frame fusion proteins with only 2/14 junctions showing imprecise repair outside coding sequences.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C15, C34-C42, C140-C143 provide strong validation evidence through complementary approaches. WGS data (C35-C37, C39) demonstrates genome-wide specificity, though one potential off-target in mNeonGreen-myosinhc could not be confirmed by PCR (C38). Sanger sequencing (C40-C41) confirms precision at junction sites. The combination of methods addresses known limitations of previous validation approaches.

results.result: Two ubiquitous nuclear marker lines (eGFP-cbx1b and mGL-cbx1b) were generated by targeting the cbx1b locus. These lines express fluorescent reporters in all nuclei of every tissue examined, serving as endogenous ubiquitous nuclear labels in teleosts.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C47 describe the generation and characterization of ubiquitous nuclear markers. The choice of cbx1b is justified by prior knowledge (C44, C45). Expression data (C47, n>10 embryos) with imaging evidence demonstrates ubiquitous nuclear labeling across tissues. The result is well-supported by both the experimental approach and characterization data.

results.result: An mScarlet-pcna fusion protein line was generated with high efficiency (28% F0 mosaic expression, 50% germline transmission). mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells were detected in supra-basal epidermal cells, with a subset showing nuclear speckles characteristic of late S phase.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C56 establish the generation and initial characterization of the mScarlet-pcna line. The rationale is supported by extensive prior work on Pcna as a proliferation marker (C49-C53). Experimental data (C54-C56, n=10 embryos) demonstrates expected expression patterns and cell cycle-specific localization (nuclear speckles in late S phase). The characterization is consistent with known Pcna biology.

results.result: An eGFP-rab11a fusion protein line was generated showing punctate intracellular signal corresponding to trafficking organelles. High expression was detected in spinal cord and neuromasts, with dynamics of intracellular organelle trafficking observed in vivo in epithelial cells and caudal fin.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C60 describe generation and characterization of the eGFP-rab11a line. The target choice is justified by prior knowledge of Rab11a function (C57). Imaging data (C58-C60, n=4-6 embryos) demonstrates expected subcellular localization and trafficking dynamics. The characterization provides 'initial evidence' (C60) of utility, appropriately cautious in interpretation.

results.result: A g3bp1-eGFP KI line was generated that shows cytoplasmic expression under normal conditions but accumulates in cytoplasmic foci (stress granules) upon temperature shock. This behavior is consistent with prior reports in other organisms and demonstrates potential as a real-time in vivo stress granule reporter.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C67 establish the g3bp1-eGFP line as a stress granule marker. The rationale is supported by prior knowledge (C62-C63). Experimental data (C64-C65, n=8 embryos) demonstrates expected stress-responsive relocalization, validated by comparison to prior work in other organisms (C66). The conclusion about potential utility (C67) is appropriately stated as inference based on initial characterization.

results.result: An mNG-myosinhc KI line was generated that exclusively labels muscle cells. The line shows correct incorporation into sarcomeres (A-bands separated by I-bands) and enables in vivo recording of endogenous Myosinhc dynamics during muscle growth for the first time in a vertebrate model.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C72 describe the mNG-myosinhc line. The target choice is justified (C69). Imaging data (C70-C71, n>10 embryos) demonstrates muscle-specific expression and correct sarcomere incorporation, validated by comparison to known sarcomere structure. Live imaging (C72, n=9 embryos) demonstrates novel capability. The claim of 'first time' (C72) is appropriately qualified with 'to the best of our knowledge.'

results.result: A cdh2-eGFP KI line was generated showing cellular membrane expression in neuronal and non-neuronal tissues including spinal cord, eye, notochord, and neuromasts. High expression in notochord cell types, not previously reported in medaka, is consistent with the tissue's mechanical stress requirements.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C79 establish the cdh2-eGFP line. The target choice is justified by prior knowledge (C73-C76). Imaging data (C77, n=5 embryos) demonstrates tissue-specific membrane expression. The novel finding of notochord expression (C78) is appropriately contextualized with mechanical stress considerations and supporting citations. Live imaging capability is demonstrated (C79, n=2 embryos).

results.result: A mapre1b-mScarlet KI line was generated showing wide expression in medaka embryos (epithelial cells, muscle, notochord, neuromasts) with highest expression in spinal cord. Microtubule dynamics in the spinal cord of living embryos were recorded.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C83 describe the mapre1b-mScarlet line. The target choice is justified by prior knowledge of microtubule plus-end binding proteins (C80). results.result: The mScarlet-pcna line acts as an organismal-wide marker for proliferative cells. In neuromasts, mScarlet-pcna expression matches the location of proliferative mantle cells (MCs) but not differentiated hair cells or support cells. Neuromast border cells (nBCs) in late S phase (4/42) were observed, providing direct evidence that nBCs retain the ability to divide.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C95 validate mScarlet-pcna as a proliferation marker in neuromasts. The experimental approach using double transgenic animals (C85) is appropriate. Expression patterns (C89-C91, n=10 neuromast organs) match prior knowledge of MC proliferation (C88, C90). The novel finding about nBC proliferation (C94-C95) is supported by observation of nuclear speckles indicating late S phase, though the sample size (4/42 cells) is modest.

results.result: Proliferative cells in the optic tectum are located at the lateral, caudal, and medial edges in a crescent-like topology with graded mScarlet-pcna expression. This pattern is consistent with previous BrdU/IdU staining studies in medaka.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C98 describe proliferation patterns in the optic tectum. Imaging data (C96-C97, n=4 embryos) demonstrates spatial organization of proliferative cells. The validation by comparison to prior histological studies (C98) strengthens the result. The characterization is well-supported and appropriately contextualized.

results.result: In the developing pectoral fin, cells located proximally expressed highest mScarlet-pcna levels with expression decreasing along the proximo-distal axis. This previously unreported pattern provides evidence that the differentiation axis is spatially organized from proximal to distal in medaka.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C100 describe a novel proliferation pattern in the pectoral fin. Imaging data (C99, n=4 embryos) demonstrates the proximo-distal gradient. The inference about differentiation axis organization (C100) is reasonable based on the proliferation gradient, though appropriately qualified as not previously reported. The sample size is modest but adequate for initial characterization.

results.result: Proliferative cells in the spinal cord of stage 40 medaka embryos occur in clusters preferentially located on the dorsal side. The mScarlet-pcna line can be used to uncover proliferation zones in vivo within organs or tissues of interest.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C102 describe spinal cord proliferation and summarize the utility of the line. Imaging data (C101, n=4 embryos) demonstrates a previously unreported finding about spinal cord proliferation. The conclusion about utility (C102) is appropriately supported by the multiple tissue characterizations presented. The result is well-supported though sample sizes are modest.

results.result: The mScarlet-pcna line recapitulates known Pcna dynamics and can be used as an endogenous cell cycle reporter. Tracked epithelial cells showed: decreasing Pcna in G1, increasing Pcna in S phase prior to nuclear speckles (late S phase marker), peak pixel intensity at S/G2 transition, and sharp decrease at M phase onset.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C111 validate mScarlet-pcna as a cell cycle reporter. The approach is grounded in extensive prior work (C103-C105, C107-C108, C110). Quantitative tracking data (C106, C109, C110, n=9 epithelial cells) demonstrates all expected cell cycle phase characteristics. The analysis methods (3D surface plots, histograms) are appropriate. The conclusion (C111) is well-supported by the comprehensive characterization matching known Pcna behavior.

results.result: CRISPR/Cas9 has been used to generate fluorescently labeled fusion proteins by HDR in various species, but HDR-mediated KI efficiencies in vertebrates can be low and the process remains cumbersome. Recent improvements include biotinylated long homology arms, linking donors to Cas9, and shorter homology arms with in vivo plasmid linearization.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C13 provide context about prior CRISPR/Cas9 work and its limitations. These are well-supported by extensive citations to prior literature. The assessment of the field (C11) is reasonable given the cited evidence. This background appropriately motivates the current work.

results.result: Despite CRISPR/Cas9's impact, there is a paucity of validated single-copy fusion protein lines in vertebrates (3 in medaka, handful in zebrafish prior to this work). Previous approaches using plasmid donors with long homology arms face challenges including concatemerization, off-target integration, and require in vivo linearization. PCR-amplified linear donors with short homology arms could be highly effective due to high molar concentration.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C120 provide field assessment and rationale for the approach. The paucity of lines (C112-C113) is documented by citations. Problems with previous approaches (C115-C119) are well-supported by extensive citations. The hypothesis about PCR-amplified donors (C120) is reasonable based on molecular considerations, though it remains a hypothesis rather than demonstrated fact.

results.result: The approach builds on recent improvements (biotinylated primers, synthetic sgRNAs, mSA-tagged Cas9) and is highly efficient, precise, and scalable. PCR amplification eliminates the need for cloning and in vivo linearization, significantly simplifying endogenous protein tagging.
results.evaluation: Claims C121-C123, C126-C128 describe methodological components and advantages. The use of established improvements (C121-C123) is well-cited. The conclusions about efficiency and simplicity (C126-C128) are supported by the experimental data showing successful generation of 8 lines with high efficiency. The advantages are clearly demonstrated by the methodology and results.

results.result: Recent work in zebrafish using a similar approach supports that donors with short homology arms are sufficient to drive HDR when in linear dsDNA form. The mechanism may involve synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA), where short homologies (30-40 bp) are sufficient to anneal with chromosomal DNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C133 provide mechanistic context and comparison to recent work. The zebrafish comparison (C129-C130) is appropriately cited and supports generalizability. The SDSA mechanism (C131-C133) is presented as a hypothesis ('one possible explanation,' C131) and is well-supported by citations to HDR mechanisms. The interpretation is appropriately cautious.

results.result: Validation of single-copy insertions is complicated with long homology arms due to concatemerization and episome formation. PCR/Sanger sequencing faces technical challenges, junction PCR can produce artifacts, and Southern blotting (the gold standard) has limitations in excluding partial integrations elsewhere. Plasmid donors can lead to unwanted insertions.
results.evaluation: Claims C134-C139 critique previous validation approaches. The limitations are well-documented by extensive citations to prior work. The assessment is balanced, acknowledging both the gold standard status of Southern blotting (C137) and its limitations (C138). This appropriately motivates the WGS validation approach used in the current work.

Ubiquitous fusion proteins from endogenous loci avoid transgene overexpression and variegation issues. The conserved cbx1b locus could provide an alternative strategy for ubiquitous nuclear markers in other teleosts and serve as a landing site for genetic constructs.

results.result: The mScarlet-pcna line addresses limitations of BrdU/IdU staining (which requires animal sacrifice) and can discover proliferation zones in any tissue. Proof-of-principle evidence shows it acts as a bona fide marker for proliferative zones in various medaka tissues, representing an important tool for stem cell research. A similar strategy could be adopted in other organisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C155-C162 discuss the significance of the mScarlet-pcna line for stem cell research. The context about stem cell research approaches (C155-C157) is well-supported by citations. The advantages over BrdU/IdU (C157-C158) are clear. The proof-of-principle evidence (C160) is supported by the multiple tissue characterizations. The conclusions about utility (C161) and potential applications (C162) are appropriately supported and qualified.

This offers advantages over FUCCI systems: no overexpression requirement, avoids variegation/silencing issues, and allows simultaneous use with other fluorescent reporters. Due to Pcna conservation, developing similar reporters in other organisms is attractive.

The advantages over FUCCI (C166-C169) are clearly articulated and appropriately supported by citations about transgene issues. The speculation about applications in other organisms (C170) is reasonable given Pcna conservation and is appropriately presented as a possibility.
